title: What Is a Problem, What Is a Solution
objectives: Break a problem down into input, process, and output
Tell the difference between a problem and a solution

hook.text: A friend asks you, "How do I make cookies with 3 cups of flour, 200 g of butter, and 2 eggs?" Is that a problem or a solution?

concept.heading: Problem and solution
concept.body: A problem is a question that needs an answer: "How do you make cookies?" A solution is the step-by-step answer to that question: the recipe itself. An algorithm is always a solution, never the problem.

concept.heading: Input, process, output
concept.body: You can split any problem into three parts: the ingredients you start with (input), what you do with them (process, or the algorithm), and what you end up with (output). In the cookie example, the input is flour, sugar, and eggs, the process is mixing and baking, and the output is the cookie itself.

exercises.question: When you withdraw money from an ATM, which of these is the "input"?
options: The thank-you message on the screen

feedback.correct: Correct. Your card and PIN are the input you give the system to start the process.
feedback.incorrect: Input is the information you give the system to start the process: your card and PIN.

exercises.question: In the same ATM example, what is the "output"?

feedback.correct: Correct. Output is the result you get at the end of the process: the banknotes.
feedback.incorrect: Output is the result you end up with when the process is done. Here, that is the banknotes.

exercises.question: Put the process that turns a problem into a solution in the correct order.
Complete the sentence.
exercises.template: A recipe is the ___ to a problem.

exercises.question: "Why is the internet slow at home?" is a problem statement. Which of these could be a solution to it?
options: Asking why the internet is slow
Restart the modem, and if it is still slow, call your provider

feedback.correct: Correct. This is a concrete solution made of steps you can actually carry out.
feedback.incorrect: A solution must contain concrete steps you can carry out, not just repeat the question or wait.

exercises.question: What is the benefit of splitting a problem into "input / process / output"?
options: It makes the problem more complicated
It clarifies what we start with and what we are aiming for

feedback.correct: Correct. This split gives you a clear frame before you start working on the solution.
feedback.incorrect: This split clarifies what we have (input) and what we want to reach (output).

summary: Problem: a question that needs an answer. Solution: the step-by-step answer to it.
Every problem can be split into input, process, and output.
An algorithm is always a solution, never the problem itself.
